applicable_when: The current launch uses XBLOCK=128 for xnumel=9, meaning cdiv(9,128)=1 block in X and 3136 blocks in Y. With 132 SMs this creates 1 full wave (132 blocks) + 1 partial wave of 3004 blocks — NCU flags this as up to 50% runtime waste. Additionally, XBLOCK=128 with xnumel=9 means 119 of 128 threads in X are masked out on every block, causing the uncoalesced access pattern (only 18/32 bytes utilized per sector). The fix is to swap the tiling strategy: use small XBLOCK (1 or 8) and large YBLOCK (32, 64, 128) so the Y dimension drives parallelism efficiently. With YBLOCK=32, grid becomes (9, 784) = 7056 blocks -> 53.5 waves, eliminating the partial-wave tail. @triton.autotune explores the best configuration automatically.
